subject: Testing Measurement Invariance over Years with Ordinal Likert Data using lavaan

messages.author: 5d76fb0f37513f01
messages.subject: Testing Measurement Invariance over Years with Ordinal Likert Data using lavaan
parts:
Hi everyone,

I’m testing measurement invariance over time (years) using lavaan.
My data consist of ordinal Likert-type items (1–4) measuring a single-factor construct, and I follow the approach recommended by Rutkowski & Svetina.

According to their guidelines for ordinal data with one factor:

  • For metric invariance, invariance is supported when:
    ΔRMSEA ≤ .05 in conjunction with significant Δχ² and ΔCFI ≥ –.004

  • For scalar invariance, invariance is supported when:
    ΔRMSEA ≤ .01 in conjunction with significant Δχ² and ΔCFI ≥ –.004

They use compareFit() (from semTools) to compare nested models.

However, to specifically test whether the chi-squared difference between models is significant, I’m using:

lavTestLRT(fit.baseline, fit.prop4)

 Is this correct ?

Thanks in advance for your help!

messages.author: 8c5a85ec8479672a
messages.subject: Re: Testing Measurement Invariance over Years with Ordinal Likert Data using lavaan
parts:
Hi, 

I am not familiar with that referenced article and don't know the specifics of your model. But to clarify: if you are checking for measurement invariance, then you are most likely comparing nested models or did I not correctly understand what you are comparing (?). 

If indeed you are comparing nested models, then, as far as I know [and looking at the source code for compareFit()], compareFit() is basically a conditional wrapper around lavTestLRT. So, both will give what you are looking for [compareFit with additional information]. 

Best, 
Felipe.
